response:
The overflow reproduces with the original binaries. The cause of the duplicate-placement problem is not what I first said, but it is reachable.

## 1. Image-request overflow

Your fixture likely never reached 64 live requests. Overflow needs more than 64 distinct live `(hash, w, h)` requests. The live set is the images still on screen or in history, plus the 16-entry `image_cache`. On the default 20x6 terminal with 40 history lines, at most 46 one-row images stay live, so it can't trigger. The 100-row resize is what makes it reachable. The clear (`ESC c`) is not required.

```python
import json, io, base64, subprocess
from PIL import Image
R = "/tmp/myterm-150-checkpoint-20261116/wezterm-checkpoint"
def png(i):
    b = io.BytesIO(); Image.new("RGBA", (1, 1), (i % 256, i // 256, 7, 255)).save(b, "PNG")
    return base64.b64encode(b.getvalue())
def img(i):  # distinct 1x1 PNG, 1 cell x 1 cell, then newline
    return b"\x1b]1337;File=inline=1;width=1;height=1:" + png(i) + b"\x07\r\n"
def run(n, tail, rows=100):
    ev = [{"resize": [20, rows]},
          {"data": list(b"".join(img(i) for i in range(n)))},
          {"data": list(tail), "checkpoint": True}]
    out = subprocess.run([R], input=json.dumps([{"name": "t", "events": ev}]).encode(),
        capture_output=True, env={"CELL_WIDTH": "9", "CELL_HEIGHT": "16"}).stdout
    c = json.loads(out)["t"]["checkpoints"][0]
    return c.get("error") or "ok"
```

Results with `python3 -I`:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| n = 10, 60, 63, 64 | ok |
| n = 65 | `image request metadata limit` |
| n = 70 with tail `ESC c` | `image request metadata limit` (stays failed after the clear) |
| n = 70 with tail `x` (no clear) | `image request metadata limit` |
| n = 70, `rows=6` | ok (never 64 live) |

The script is `/tmp/review-wz/min.py`. The overflow is set while storing the 65th live request, and nothing resets it. The `ESC c` row is the sticky case. After the clear nothing is live, yet every later checkpoint still fails.

## 2. Duplicate `id:placement` across buffers

It is reachable with real input, not an invented envelope. The behaviour differs from what I first wrote. The native Swift reference replaces the placement record, so it keeps one record for a given `(id, placement)`, owned by the latest placement. The importer keeps the first one it sees (the normal buffer). So the restored record has the wrong buffer, position and column/row.

Sequence (`up` transmits a 1x1 RGBA image with `i=1`). After `up`, place `ESC_Ga=p,i=1,p=1,c=2,r=1;ESC\` on the normal buffer. Then send `ESC[?1049h ESC[H`, place the same ids again, checkpoint, and send `!`. The script is `/tmp/review-wz/dup.py`.

| Case | Native reference placements `(img, place, isAlt, col, row)` | Restored from checkpoint |
|---|---|---|
| Same ids, both buffers | `[(1, 1, True, 0, 0)]` | `[(1, 1, False, 0, 0)]` |
| Same ids, the second placed after `ESC[3;5H` | `[(1, 1, True, 4, 2)]` | `[(1, 1, False, 0, 0)]` |
| Different placement ids (control) | both records present | identical to the reference |

Rust exports image cells for both buffers, because the ids sit on the cells of both screens. Only the importer's `placementKeys` dedup (`CheckpointBridge.swift:270-278`) picks the wrong one. The imported cells and images are probably right; the `kitty.placements` table is what differs.

**Impact:** a later `a=d` delete by id or a placement query would act on the wrong buffer. I did not run that follow-up, so that part is inferred.

**Fix direction:** the importer should keep the last record in scan order, matching native replace semantics, instead of first-wins.

I did not edit files, run a GUI or read unrelated files, and I'm not judging the in-progress fixes.
